edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Referunt aliquando dictum a quadam, cum primum quaestio ista tentata est: Et quomodo caeteras sollicitabimus ad hujusmodi opus. Scilicet felices nos facient, si plures erunt, et non Dei gratia vel merita cujusque. Virgines ecclesiam, an ecclesia virgines ornat Deo, sive commendat? Confessa est igitur gloriam esse in caussa. Porro ubi gloria, illic sollicitatio; ubi sollicitatio, illic coactio; ubi coactio, illic necessitas; ubi necessitas, illic infirmitas. Merito itaque dum caput non tegunt ut sollicitentur gloriae caussa, ventres tegere coguntur infirmitatis ruina. Aemulatio enim illas, non religio producit: aliquando et ipse venter Deus earum, quia facile virginis fraternitas suscipit. Nec tantum autem ruunt, sed et funem longum delictorum sibi adtrabunt. Prolatae enim in medium, et publicato bono suo elatae, et a fratribus omni honore et caritatis operatione cumulatae, dum non latent ubi quid admissum est, tantum dedecoris cogitant, quantum honoris habuerunt. Si intectum caput virginitati adscribitur, si qua virgo exciderit de gratia virginitatis, ne prodatur, intecto permanet capite: et tunc jam alieno ambulat habitu, id est quem sibi vindicat virginitas: permanet nihilominus in habitu, vel tunc saltem alieno, ne scilicet mutatione prodatur. Consciae mulieritatis jam indubitatae, audent nudo capite ad Deum adire. Sed aemulator Deus et Dominus, qui dixit: Nihil occultum quod non revelabitur, plerasque etiam in conspectum deducit. Non enim confitebuntur, nisi ipsorum infantium suorum vagitibus proditae. Quantum autem plures, non etiam de pluribus sceleribus suspectas habebis? Dicam, licet nolim, difficile mulier semel fit, quae non timet fieri, quaeque jam facta potest virginem mentiri sub Deo. Quanta item circa uterum suum audebit, ne etiam mater detegatur! Scit Deus quod jam infantes et perfici et perduci ad partum integros duxerit, debellatos aliquandiu a matribus. Facillime semper concipiunt, et felicissime pariunt hujusmodi virgines, et quidem simillimos patribus. Haec admittit flagitia coacta et invita virginitas. Ipsa concupiscentia non latendi non est pudica, patitur aliquid quod virginis non sit, studium placendi, utique et viris. Quantum velis bona mente conetur, necesse est publicatione sui periclitetur, dum percutitur oculis incertis et multis, dum digitis demonstrantium titillatur, dum nimium amatur, dum inter amplexus et oscula assidua concalescit. Sic frons duratur, sic pudor teritur, sic solvitur, sic discitur aliter jam placere desiderare.
pass_a_gloss: They sometimes report a statement made by a certain person, when this question was first attempted: And how will we solicit the others to this kind of work? Certainly, they will make us happy, if there are more of them, and not by the grace of God or the merits of each one. Do virgins adorn the church for God, or does the church commend the virgins? Therefore, it is confessed that there is glory in the cause. Furthermore, where there is glory, there is solicitation; where there is solicitation, there is coercion; where there is coercion, there is necessity; where there is necessity, there is weakness. Therefore, while they do not cover their head in order to be solicited for the sake of glory, they are forced to cover their bellies due to the ruin of weakness. For emulation, not religion, produces them: sometimes even their own belly is their god, because the sisterhood of virgins easily accepts it. And they not only rush into it, but they also draw upon themselves a long rope of sins. For when they are put forward in public and their good is proclaimed, and they are heaped with every honor and work of charity by the brothers, while they do not hide where something has been admitted, they think of as much shame as they had honor. If an uncovered head is ascribed to virginity, if any virgin falls from the grace of virginity, in order not to be betrayed, she remains with an uncovered head: and then she already walks in a foreign habit, that is, the one that virginity claims for herself: nonetheless, she remains in the habit, or at least a foreign one, so that she may not be betrayed by a change. Conscious of their womanhood, already undisputed, they dare to approach God with an uncovered head. But God and the Lord is a rival, who said: Nothing hidden will not be revealed, and He leads many into the public eye. For they will not confess, unless they are betrayed by the cries of their own infants. How much more, the more numerous they are, will you not also suspect them of more crimes? I will say, although I do not want to, it is difficult for a woman to become one who does not fear to become, and who, already having become, can lie about being a virgin under God. How much will she dare to do around her own womb, lest even the mother be revealed! God knows that already infants are led to birth intact, having been conquered for a time by their mothers. These kinds of virgins always conceive very easily and give birth very happily, and indeed they produce children very similar to their fathers. This forced and unwilling virginity admits to shameful acts. The very desire not to hide is not modest, it suffers something that is not suitable for a virgin, the desire to please, certainly even men. However much she tries with a good mind, it is necessary that she be endangered by the publication of herself, while she is struck by uncertain and numerous eyes, while she is titillated by pointing fingers, while she is loved too much, while she grows warm among frequent embraces and kisses. Thus the forehead is hardened, thus modesty is worn away, thus it is dissolved, thus it is learned to desire to please in a different way.

pass_b_english: People still repeat what a certain woman said when this question was first raised: "And how will we get the others to sign on for this kind of work?" They will make us happy, if there are more of them, and not by the grace of God or the merits of each one. Do virgins adorn the church for God, or does the church commend the virgins? So it is admitted that the whole enterprise is about glory. And where there is glory, there is recruitment; where there is recruitment, there is coercion; where there is coercion, there is necessity; where there is necessity, there is weakness. So while they leave their heads uncovered in order to be recruited for the sake of glory, they end up forced to cover their bellies because weakness has ruined them. Rivalry produces these women, not religion: sometimes even their own belly is their god, because the sisterhood of virgins easily accepts it. And they do not just rush into it; they also drag a long rope of sins behind them. For when they are put on public display and their virtue is proclaimed, and the brothers heap every honor and work of charity on them, while they cannot hide where something has been admitted, they feel as much shame as they once had honor. If an uncovered head is the badge of virginity, and a virgin falls from the grace of virginity, she keeps her head uncovered so she will not be exposed — and at that point she is already walking in a habit that belongs to someone else, the one that virginity claims for itself. She stays in the habit anyway, or at least in a borrowed one, so that a change of clothing does not betray her. Conscious of a womanhood that is now undeniable, they dare to approach God with uncovered heads. But God and the Lord is a rival who said: "Nothing is hidden that will not be revealed" (Luke 8:17), and he drags many of them into the open. They will not confess unless the cries of their own infants betray them. The more of them there are, the more you must suspect them of greater crimes. I will say it, though I do not want to: it is hard for a woman to become someone who does not fear becoming pregnant, and who, once she has, can lie about being a virgin under God. How far will she go to hide what happens in her own womb, so that even the mother stays concealed? God knows that infants have already been brought to birth intact, after being fought off for a time by their mothers. These virgins always conceive very easily and give birth very happily, and the children look just like their fathers. This forced, unwilling virginity admits to shameful acts. The very desire not to stay hidden is not modest; it endures something unworthy of a virgin — the desire to please, certainly even men. However much she tries with a good mind, she must risk herself by being put on display, while she is struck by uncertain and countless eyes, while she is titillated by pointing fingers, while she is loved too much, while she grows warm among constant embraces and kisses. Thus the forehead is hardened, thus modesty is worn away, thus it is dissolved, thus she learns to desire to please in a different way.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and meaning of the source. Pass B provides a fluent English rendering that remains faithful to the Latin. The scripture citation (Luke 8:17) added in Pass B for 'Nihil occultum quod non revelabitur' is a correct identification of the allusion.
